decision: Memoize the compositor surface so the window plane's re-renders stop at it
why: This is the cause of every compositor effect flashing during a drag. The surface re-rendered on every store change, each render re-attached the canvas ref, and useConfigureContext disconnects and constructs a new ResizeObserver for each attach. A newly observed element always gets one callback, and that callback writes canvas.width, which resets the canvas and drops its WebGPU swap chain. The result is a blank frame with no error and correct data. @typegpu/react documents that per-frame values go through useFrame and .write() and never through a React render; the surface already reads the store with state$.peek() inside useFrame, so it needs no render of its own
evidence: Wrapped ResizeObserver and the canvas width setter on the live page. Before: a 30-frame drag constructed 60 observers, fired 29 callbacks and wrote canvas.width 29 times. After: 0, 0 and 0, with the backing size still 2300x1346
result: VERIFIED: owner confirmed the flashing is gone on the earlier workaround, and this root-cause fix reproduces that with the library's own autoResize left on. No upstream deficit; the earlier claim of one was wrong

decision: Rewrite backend/surface.tsx from scratch on the documented @typegpu/react and TypeGPU patterns: pipelines in useMemo, one useFrame, no useEffect, no useState, no readiness gate, no destroy hooks, and per-draw bare submissions via pipeline.withColorAttachment(target()).draw(n) with the first claim clearing and later claims loading
why: The owner required the file reworked from first principles. The old file mutated a ref during render, drove pass construction through useState so a teardown left a frame with zero passes, hand-rolled a dirty flag over the store's own reactivity, gated drawing behind Promise.allSettled and a cancelled flag, and hand-rolled a shared command encoder. TypeGPU's pipelines page documents loadOp clear then load for several pipelines on one canvas and states pipelines compile lazily on first draw, so the readiness gate had no basis
evidence: docs.swmansion.com/TypeGPU/apis/pipelines and the @typegpu/react README; renderPipeline.d.ts withColorAttachment; framework, playground, and Polkadot all type-check with zero errors; all three API gates pass
result: VERIFIED structurally by type-check and gates. The rewrite alone did NOT fix the flashing; the canvas reset above did

decision: Drive the contact shadow from each window's height in the stack: shadow lift, spread and faintness all scale with the normalized z already carried in WindowInstance.state.w, and each window casts its own shadow with the nearest winning instead of one union shaded once
why: The owner states the canvas is a world with depth and everything on it is diegetic. Depth is already uploaded per window as state.w, 0 at the back and 1 at the front, and no pass read it: radiance, focus field and contact shadow all treated every window as coplanar. The shadow offset every window by the same 6 pixels with the same softness, which is the CSS drop-shadow idiom rather than a depth cue

decision: Revise the scene-model spine to revision 2: split intent from state. The store says what the world should become; a GPU-resident world holds what it is and moves toward the intent by dt in one compute step before any pass draws. Window height becomes a world coordinate. Delete rather than tune the radiance pass, WindowInstance.state.w and InfiniteCanvasScenePass.frameloop
why: The owner states the canvas is a world with depth where everything is diegetic, and reports light changing instantly on focus. Revision 1 declared the scene model a pure derivation from state, which is the architecture the compositor already has. A pure projection of the current state has no previous value to move from, so continuity is unreachable in it; and its windows are rects with a stacking index, so depth is nominal. Radiance cascades solves a 2D field whose sdf and color hooks take a flat uv, so height cannot reach the lighting through its API
evidence: apps/compositor-poc/src/spine/scene-model-spine.tsx revision 2; surface.tsx rebuilds every frame from store.state$.peek(); instances.ts writes tint.w from a boolean so emission is a step function; the runner's own getCascadeDim and 2D uv hooks in node_modules/@typegpu/radiance-cascades
result: NOT VERIFIED: this is a spine revision, not production code. It supersedes revision 1 and needs review before any production write follows it. The lighting technique for a world with depth is deliberately left open as backlog item 7

decision: Build the world in production: compositor/backend/world.ts holds a GPU-resident body per window and one compute step moves it toward the document by dt before any pass draws. The surface uploads targets to a separate buffer and binds the instances accessor to the body buffer, so every pass reads the settled world with no pass edited
